quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the train has passed.
No, never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers are doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. Warning signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train horn. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
Just one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street to another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The middle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder with no one in it.
Whenever it approaches you, even without flashing lights.
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights stopped to pick up or drop off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What does this warning sign mean?

options.text: The right lane is ending. Move left.
The road curves ahead.
Intersections are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending. Move left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns that one lane is ending and you need to merge left.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn around and look out the back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: You should check your rearview mirror regularly to know where traffic behind you is located.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks and always obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: Your car starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the car to go. If the rear slides left, steer left. This brings the front and rear in line and straightens out your car.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision decreases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means greater impairment.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead ends.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. No passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: Which of these increases a driver's crash risk the most?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you from driving and increase crash risk.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive as you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change speed and direction slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may slide and you could lose control.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
You can pick up or drop off passengers.
No parking, stopping, or standing.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, stopping, or standing.
questions.explanation: A red curb means you cannot park, stop, or stand there.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road ahead has curves. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic and pass only when necessary.
Get in front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic and pass only when necessary.
questions.explanation: Every pass increases crash risk. Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed. Do not pass more than necessary.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds above 35 mph, tires lose the ability to push water away. Your tires can then ride over water like skis and lose grip on the road.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Follow it closely to save fuel.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signals while parking at a curb?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals both when approaching the curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and others around you is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Extra space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach the intersection. Let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: You must report an accident if there is ____ or more in damage to someone's property.
questions.explanation: Report an accident to police if someone is hurt, someone dies, or damage is $1,000 or more. You must also report if damage to government property (like signs) is $200 or more.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower your blood alcohol level (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else can speed this up, including eating and drinking.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, drive:

options.text: At or near the freeway traffic speed.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: Neither direction may pass.
Both directions may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither direction may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic going opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: You park facing downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car rolls away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with no curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your stopping ability. Poor road conditions require you to slow down to control your vehicle. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop and puts you at risk.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass until after you pass the sign.
Do not pass unless it seems safe.
Do not pass for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass for any reason.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign shows a rule you must obey. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right lane immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, move back to your lane when you have enough space between your car and the car you passed.

questions.question: How should you handle tailgaters?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If a car is following too closely, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What should you do when in a travel lane?

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance.
Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road. If you miss your exit, go to the next one instead of backing up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a roundabout coming up. Enter at a low speed and yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What do orange background signs mean?

options.text: General warning signs.
Construction and maintenance warning signs.
Regulatory signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are only used for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: What do highway markings do?

options.text: They are usually not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They provide information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers information. They show where to position your vehicle, mark safe passing zones, and warn of upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should you NOT use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using a horn near blind pedestrians can be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Your driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates other drivers, causing them to make unsafe passing attempts. Drive with the flow of traffic and within the speed limit.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection if there are no oncoming vehicles
Only where signs and road markings allow passing
On a curve if there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Only where signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections or near parking lot entrances. If your view is blocked by a curve or hill, stay in your lane. Assume another vehicle may be coming. Only pass where signs and road markings say it is allowed, and only if you have enough safe space.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, stay farther away from the car in front of you. Use your headlights to help you see. Follow the rules about when to use high beams and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the brightness can blind you.

questions.question: What blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at an accident.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at an accident.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents stops traffic flow and should be avoided. This is called rubbernecking and causes traffic jams.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed on the side with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed on the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: What should you know about driving on gravel or dirt roads?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires do not grip as well as on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires do not grip as well as on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires do not grip loose gravel and dirt as well as they grip pavement. You must slow down because stopping takes longer and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following the car ahead too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to hitting other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed constant.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What color lines divide lanes moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid being hit by the tailgater. Do not brake suddenly.
